# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [insert date this letter is sent]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
**Fax:** 859-425-3379
**Mail:** [insert appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-07**
- **Member:** Morgan Grant
- **Member ID:** W585722922
- **Reference number:** POC-8EE886247D-14307
- **Denied service:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
- **Requesting surgeon:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Aetna's decision to deny prior authorization for the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) that my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has requested and documented as medically necessary for me. The notice dated 2026-08-07 states that the procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, because the records already submitted match the plan's own published criteria in **Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty**, which I quote below.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. The plan's policy states:**

> "Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint; and"

My records establish this. I have had 9 months of progressive pain in the knee that is not relieved by rest. I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3–4 times every night because of the pain.

**2. The plan's policy states:**

> "Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination: and"

My records establish this. On examination, my range of motion is limited by pain, and provocative testing was positive on the affected side. I note that this criterion as published ends in a colon and appears to introduce further detail that was not provided to me. If Aetna applied any additional element here, I ask that it be identified specifically.

**3. The plan's policy states:**

> "Patient's knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) is not limited to 90 degrees or less; and"

My records document that my range of motion is limited by pain. They do not contain a measurement in degrees. I ask that Dr. Okafor's examination findings be reviewed on this point, and I am requesting that my surgeon's office supply the measured arc of motion: [insert measured arc of motion in degrees from Dr. Okafor's exam note, if available].

**4. The plan's policy states:**

> "Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) (see Appendix ) affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint; and"

My records establish this directly. My MRI of the knee dated 2026-07-06 shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially — a single compartment, which is precisely the finding this criterion describes and the reason a partial rather than total replacement was requested.

**5. Conservative care.** The plan's policy states:

> "History of of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record (see Note Footnote3 *** ) with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy)."

and:

> "Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."

Here is what my record shows, exactly:

- Supervised, in-person physical therapy with a licensed physical therapist, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion: **8 weeks, from 2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07, 16 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This is formal, in-person therapy — not home or virtual — and it is confirmed by the actual PT note, as the policy allows.
- NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-25, which gave only about 2 weeks of partial relief.

The plan's excerpt above refers to "12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI" but does not state which duration applies to a member with my age and BMI (my BMI is documented as 29), and I have not been told which figure Aetna applied to me. I ask Aetna to identify the specific duration it required and the basis for choosing it.

I also ask Aetna to apply its own exception, which appears in the same policy:

> "Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral); and"

My imaging shows exactly that situation: bone-on-bone apposition in the **medial** compartment — a weight-bearing compartment, not the patellofemoral compartment — with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 disease. Under the plan's own language, further conservative therapy may be inappropriate in this circumstance. If Aetna denied my request because of the length of my physical therapy, I ask the reviewer to address this sentence of the policy directly and explain why it was not applied to my documented bone-on-bone medial findings.

**6. The individual components of non-surgical management.** The plan's policy lists:

> "Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and"

> "Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; and"

> "Activity modification; and"

> "Supervised physical therapy (activities of daily living [ADLs] diminished despite completing a plan of care); and"

My records address these: NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief; physical therapy directed at quadriceps strengthening and range of motion; and 16 completed supervised PT visits after which I still cannot climb stairs without assistance and still wake 3–4 times nightly with pain — that is, my activities of daily living remain diminished despite completing a plan of care, which is what this criterion describes. For activity modification, please see [insert documentation of activity modification from the medical record, if available].

**7. Items the policy makes optional for me.** The plan's policy states:

> "Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote4 † to joint replacement, optional for others); and"

> "Therapeutic injections into the knee (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote4 † to joint replacement, optional for others)."

Nothing in my records identifies a relative contraindication to joint replacement: I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker. On the plan's own terms, these two items are therefore optional in my case — and I nonetheless had a therapeutic corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-25, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. I ask that the absence of an assistive-device trial not be used as a reason to deny my surgery when the policy itself makes it optional.

**8. Co-morbidities and diabetes.** The plan's policy states:

> "For members with significant conditions or co-morbidities, the risk/benefit of unicompartmental knee arthroplasty should be appropriately addressed in the medical record."

and:

> "If member is diabetic, their hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to knee arthroplasty."

The records submitted for me do not identify diabetes, active infection, untreated substance use, or smoking. If Aetna considers this HbA1c criterion applicable to me, I ask that it say so, and I will provide: [insert HbA1c result and date, if applicable].

**9. The plan's policy states:**

> "Member must have intact, stable ligaments, in particular the anterior cruciate ligament; and"

My submitted records do not include a statement about ligament stability. Rather than have this treated as a failure, I am asking my surgeon's office to supply it: [insert Dr. Okafor's documentation of ligament and ACL stability]. If ligament status is the basis of the denial, I ask Aetna to state that plainly so it can be answered with one document.

## What I am asking for

The excerpts above are the only portions of Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty that I have been given, and some of them clearly introduce further conditions that were not reproduced for me. I therefore also ask Aetna, as part of this appeal, to identify in writing the specific criterion or criteria from this policy that my request was found not to meet.

Please:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-07 (reference POC-8EE886247D-14307) and authorize CPT 27446 as requested by Dr. Okafor;
2. Have my appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer with orthopedic expertise; and
3. Provide me with a copy of the complete clinical criteria and the reviewer's rationale applied to my case.

I am submitting this appeal with Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, by fax to 859-425-3379 and/or to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date, **by 2027-02-03**, and this appeal is submitted within that period.

Enclosed for the reviewer's file: [list enclosures — e.g., denial notice dated 2026-08-07; physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07; MRI report dated 2026-07-06; Dr. Okafor's office and operative-planning notes; medication and injection records].

Thank you for reviewing my case again. My surgeon has documented why this operation is needed, and I would very much like to move forward with it.

Sincerely,

**[Signature]**

Morgan Grant
Member ID: W585722922
Date of birth: [insert date of birth]
Address: [insert street address, city, MA, ZIP]
Phone: [insert phone number]
Email: [insert email address]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
